title: The ordinary closed-fibre unit germ is the canonical local-acyclicity map
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a scheme morphism [def-pc-scheme], $G$ an abelian etale sheaf on $X$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], and $s:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to S$ and $t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'\to S_{(s)}$ geometric points [def-weil-geometric-point, def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Put $p:X'=X\times_SS_{(s)}\to X$ and let $i:X_s\to X'$ and $h:X_t\to X'$ be the canonical fibre projections [def-pc-fibre-product, lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality]. Write $K=p^{-1}G$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and let $\beta:K\to h_*h^{-1}K$ be the ordinary sheaf adjunction unit [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. At any geometric $z$ of $X_s$, put $x=p\circ i\circ z$ and let $a$ be the $z$-stalk of $i^{-1}\beta$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. There exist an isomorphism $e:S_{(s)}\simeq S_{(f\circ x)}$, an isomorphism $A$ from the source of $a$ to $G_x$, and an isomorphism $B$ from the target of $a$ to $\Gamma(V_{f,x,e\circ t},G|_V)$ [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor], such that $B\circ a=\alpha_{G,x,e\circ t}\circ A$ [def-weil-pbc-local-acyclicity-abelian-sheaf]. Here $G|_V$ is inverse image along $V_{f,x,e\circ t}\to X_{(x)}\to X$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. No local acyclicity hypothesis is imposed. This equality compares the actual morphisms, rather than merely their source and target objects.

proof.text: Choose the canonical pointed strict-local map q from the localization of iz on X' to that of x on X. The strict-base closed-point localizations theorem makes q invertible and gives e and the fibre isomorphism over X. The inverse-image stalk comparison for i, canonical strict-local restriction of K, coefficient composition along q, inverse pullback of global sections along q, and inverse canonical restriction of G define A. This choice of A avoids needing a separate naturality theorem for restriction under the morphism p.

proof.text: The map t is between affine schemes, so its base change h is affine and hence qcqs. Apply the unrestricted strict-henselization stalk theorem in degree zero to h and h-inverse-image K, retaining its actual canonical restriction composite. Transport through the left-exact degree-zero comparison and the single-complex/global-sections comparison. The degree-zero adjunction-unit normalization, its naturality, and the mate formula identify this canonical composite with r_(h_*h-inverse-image K) followed by ordinary exchange on strict-local sections and the direct-image global-sections isomorphism. It is therefore invertible. The fibre isomorphism and inverse-image coefficient composition over X then define B. Mere existence of an object-level target-stalk isomorphism is not sufficient here; use the canonical map in the unrestricted theorem.

proof.text: Canonical strict-local restriction is natural in the sheaf: precompose with representative affine pointed-neighbourhood germs, use strictHenselizationSectionRestriction_naturality, then use their colimit universal property. Apply this naturality to the ordinary unit. The base-change identity map_unit_baseChangeMap_app changes its pullback followed by the ordinary exchange map into the fibre-projection unit followed by the inverse-image square comparison. On global sections this is pullback to the strict-local fibre; strictLocalUnderivedMateSections_eq verifies the same formula on each pointed representative. Transport along q and the fibre isomorphism over X. Functoriality of global-sections pullback and the inverse-image composition-unit identity give exactly alpha after the chosen A. Equality on representative germs proves the displayed equality. Neither local acyclicity nor a vanishing assertion is used; zero sheaves and empty fibres are included.

theorem closedFibre_unit_stalk_comparison
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    (G : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1})
    {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S)
    {Ω' : Type u} [Field Ω'] [IsAlgClosed Ω']
    (t : Spec (.of Ω') ⟶ Scheme.strictHenselizationScheme s)
    {Ξ : Type u} [Field Ξ] [IsAlgClosed Ξ]
    (z : Spec (.of Ξ) ⟶
      pullback (pullback.snd f (Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap s))
        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Scheme.strictHenselizationPointEvaluation s)))) :
    let p := pullback.fst f (Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap s)
    let f' := pullback.snd f (Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap s)
    let i := pullback.fst f' (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom
      (Scheme.strictHenselizationPointEvaluation s)))
    let h := pullback.fst f' t
    let x := (z ≫ i) ≫ p
    let K := (upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} p).obj G
    let β := (upperStarLowerStarAdjunction AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} h).unit.app K
    let a := (Scheme.pointSmallEtale z).sheafFiber.map
      ((upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} i).map β)
    ∃ e : Scheme.strictHenselizationScheme s ≅ Scheme.strictHenselizationScheme (x ≫ f),
      ∃ A : (Scheme.pointSmallEtale z).sheafFiber.obj
          ((upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} i).obj K) ≅
          (Scheme.pointSmallEtale x).sheafFiber.obj G,
        ∃ B : (Scheme.pointSmallEtale z).sheafFiber.obj
            ((upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} i).obj
              (((upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} h) ⋙
                (lowerStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1} h)).obj K)) ≅
            (Sheaf.Γ (localAcyclicityFiber f x (t ≫ e.hom)).smallEtaleTopology
              AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}).obj
              ((upperStar AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}
                (pullback.fst (localAcyclicityStrictMap f x) (t ≫ e.hom) ≫
                  Scheme.strictHenselizationStructuralMap x)).obj G),
          a ≫ B.hom = A.hom ≫ localAcyclicityAlpha f x (t ≫ e.hom) G
